programme: Twelve-week Ledger API, Platform & Reliability Engineering

assumptions.api_experience: Assume no current API-building experience and no reliable recall of FastAPI; teach HTTP and API design first, then build the app step by step.
assumptions.python_experience: Do not schedule Python fundamentals. Assume the learner knows Python and can read/write ordinary application code; only cover environment and dependency setup as needed for the project.
assumptions.optional_extensions: Selected sessions include an optional 15-minute stretch; never required.
assumptions.project_approach: Start with the request/response model and endpoint contract before implementing routes. Avoid large code dumps; build one endpoint at a time and explain each decision.
assumptions.project_domain: Build a simulated double-entry ledger API, not a generic task manager. No real funds or payment rails.
assumptions.database: Use PostgreSQL for the main application. SQLite is not part of the application architecture.
assumptions.git_and_publishing: Use local Git during development. Publish source and enable GitHub Actions at the planned source-control/CI milestone, not on Day 1.
assumptions.observability: Prometheus and Grafana are core. Structured stdout logs are core. Loki/Alloy and OpenTelemetry/Jaeger are optional extensions.
assumptions.cloud: The AWS exercise is temporary and cost-controlled. Never assume a free tier; estimate costs before apply, use minimal resources and verify destroy/cleanup.
assumptions.interview_practice: DSA is a separate optional 15-minute side track twice per week; it does not displace the 60-minute core session.

cadence.first_week_exception: Start Tuesday 24 November 2026; Week 1 has five study sessions (Tuesday–Saturday). Sundays remain review/rest days.

days.title: API lab setup and first FastAPI process
days.objective: Verify the existing Colima/Docker setup without changing it; check Python/Git versions; create the reliability-lab-api folder and virtual environment; install FastAPI; create a minimal app and run it locally.
days.deliverable: A minimal FastAPI application running locally, a clean project folder, .venv excluded from Git, and /docs opening in the browser.
days.notes: Completed and verified interactively. Colima started successfully; Docker uses the colima context and the Docker CLI discovers the Homebrew Compose plugin. Python 3.14.2 and Git 2.56.1 available. Created reliability-lab-api with an active .venv, .gitignore excluding .venv and Python cache files, and installed FastAPI 0.165.0 (fastapi[standard]). Created main.py with GET / returning {"message":"Hello, world!"}. FastAPI dev server started at http://127.0.0.1:8000; terminal logs confirm GET /, /docs, and /openapi.json returned HTTP 200. favicon.ico 404 is harmless.

check Python/Git versions
create the reliability-lab-api folder and virtual environment
install FastAPI
create a minimal app and run it locally.

days.title: HTTP request and response anatomy for account and transfer APIs
days.objective: Understand client/server request and response anatomy using GET /accounts and POST /transfers; identify method, path, headers, body, status and JSON response.

days.extension_task: Compare the same request with and without an Accept header using curl.

Inspect Content-Type, Accept and Idempotency-Key headers

Distinguish safe and idempotent HTTP methods

days.title: HTTP status codes and financial API errors

days.deliverable: A status-code decision table for account and transfer operations.
tasks: Review 2xx, 4xx and 5xx status groups
Choose responses for invalid input and missing accounts
Distinguish insufficient funds from unexpected server failure

migration_note: Revised on 2026-11-23 after learner clarified that Python fundamentals are not needed. Week 1 now covers HTTP/API foundations; Week 2 starts FastAPI directly. No previously completed sessions existed; all 60 sessions remain not_started. Further updated the Week 6–10 lab overlay on 2026-11-23 to add free browser labs paired with local Colima/k3d work, Docker networking, Loki/Alloy logs, OpenTelemetry/Jaeger traces and three explicit incident drills. Existing progress statuses and notes were preserved. Rebased on 2026-11-23 for a Tuesday 2026-11-24 start. Sundays remain review/rest days. Week 1 is a five-session kickoff; Weeks 2–12 each contain six sessions. Added 11 consolidation sessions D61–D71. Existing session statuses were preserved as not_started; finish moved to 2027-02-13 and final review to 2027-02-14. Revised on 2026-11-24 after external review: changed generic Task API to a simulated double-entry Ledger API; replaced SQLite with PostgreSQL; added idempotency, atomic transfers, concurrency, Alembic, CI/CD, Terraform, a cost-controlled AWS EC2 deployment, Linux host/network troubleshooting and SLO burn-rate alerts. Prometheus/Grafana are core; Loki/Alloy and OpenTelemetry/Jaeger are optional. Added a separate two-times-weekly DSA side track outside core sessions. Preserved 71 session dates, review cadence, optional extension totals and prior completion evidence.
lab_method: For D31-D48 use short browser Docker/Kubernetes/Linux labs as a supplement and reproduce key behaviour locally through Colima/k3d. D49-D71 focus on GitHub Actions, Terraform, controlled cloud deployment, Prometheus/Grafana and independent troubleshooting. Browser labs are disposable; save evidence in the local project.
browser_lab_safety: Do not enter production credentials, AWS keys, tokens or personal data into public labs. Browser scenarios are disposable and may reset. Use fake database passwords in local examples.
observability_signals: core metrics: Prometheus request/latency/transfer metrics and PromQL
core dashboards/alerts: Grafana with SLO and multi-window burn-rate alerting
core logs: structured application stdout and Docker/Kubernetes/cloud log inspection
optional log aggregation: Grafana Alloy and Loki
aws_lab_safety: AWS resources can incur charges and free-tier eligibility is not guaranteed. Review AWS Pricing Calculator, restrict inbound access, avoid NAT gateways/load balancers/managed Kubernetes for this lab, set a time/spend limit, run terraform destroy and verify cleanup. Never paste credentials into chat or commit secrets or Terraform state.
